decision.purpose: Production refresh-intent delivery for Spring Cloud Config through Spring Cloud Bus with the Kafka binder
decision.payloadPolicy: Events contain application and revision routing metadata only; secrets and configuration values are forbidden

requiredApprovals.topicNameStrategy: One pre-provisioned topic per environment and region: platform.config.bus.<environment>.<region>. Dynamic destinations and application-created topics are forbidden
requiredApprovals.environmentIsolation: Production and non-production use separate Kafka clusters where available and always use separate topics, principals, consumer groups and ACLs. No principal receives access across environment boundaries
requiredApprovals.producerPrincipal: Dedicated Config Server workload identity. WRITE and DESCRIBE are limited to the exact environment/region Bus topic. CREATE, ALTER, DELETE and wildcard topic permissions are forbidden
requiredApprovals.consumerPrincipal: Dedicated workload identity per deployed service. READ and DESCRIBE are limited to the exact environment/region Bus topic and READ is limited to instance-scoped consumer groups. WRITE is forbidden because Bus acknowledgements, tracing, environment mutation and shutdown events are disabled
requiredApprovals.aclModel: Default deny and least privilege. Kafka administrators pre-provision topics and ACLs. Config Server receives topic WRITE/DESCRIBE; service identities receive topic READ/DESCRIBE and group READ for the approved instance-group prefix; platform operations receive read-only diagnostics separately. Prefix or wildcard ACLs spanning environments are forbidden
requiredApprovals.authentication: SASL_SSL with short-lived corporate workload identity. OAUTHBEARER is the preferred SASL mechanism; SCRAM-SHA-512 requires an explicit security exception and managed secret rotation. SASL_PLAINTEXT and anonymous access are forbidden
requiredApprovals.transportEncryption: TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred, hostname verification enabled, corporate CA trust, certificate and credential rotation without application image changes, and no plaintext listener fallback
requiredApprovals.retention: cleanup.policy=delete; retention.ms=86400000 (24 hours); retention.bytes is bounded by the Kafka platform quota. Startup always reloads the latest complete configuration snapshot, so retained events are not an authoritative state store
requiredApprovals.partitioning: Six partitions initially, replication.factor=3, min.insync.replicas=2, unclean leader election disabled, producer acks=all and enable.idempotence=true. Capacity review may increase partitions; consumers must not depend on cross-partition ordering
requiredApprovals.serviceIdUniqueness: Set spring.cloud.bus.id to <spring.application.name>:<environment>-<region>:<immutable-instance-id>. Kubernetes uses pod UID as the immutable instance ID. Startup fails when environment, region or immutable instance ID is absent
requiredApprovals.multiInstanceBehavior: Every application instance uses a unique Bus ID and an instance-scoped consumer group so every live instance receives each refresh intent. A shared service-level Kafka consumer group is forbidden because it would load-balance an event to only one instance. Duplicate and out-of-order delivery is accepted and must coalesce to UNCHANGED or STALE
requiredApprovals.incidentOwner: Platform Configuration Control Plane Team is service owner; Corporate Kafka Platform Team owns broker incidents; service teams own client connectivity. Alerts route through the central production incident process with both platform teams on escalation

monitorSecurity.authentication: The source-code provider authenticates to a dedicated private webhook ingress using mTLS or a provider-specific HMAC secret stored in the corporate secret manager. Static bearer tokens and unauthenticated POST requests are forbidden
monitorSecurity.authorization: Only the dedicated repository webhook identity may invoke POST /monitor. Interactive users, application service identities and public Actuator access are denied. Bus refresh, bus environment and bus shutdown Actuator endpoints remain disabled
monitorSecurity.ingressRestriction: POST /monitor is exposed only through the control-plane ingress, never through an application or public Actuator ingress. Enforce source network allowlists where the provider publishes stable ranges, WAF request-size limits, TLS and a deny-by-default route policy
monitorSecurity.webhookVerification: Verify the signature over the unmodified request body using a constant-time comparison before Spring Cloud Config handles the event. Require the expected event type and allowlisted repository, organization and branch/ref. Reject missing, malformed or unverifiable metadata
monitorSecurity.replayProtection: Require a provider delivery ID and cache accepted IDs for 24 hours in a shared bounded store. Reject duplicate delivery IDs. Enforce a five-minute timestamp window when the provider signs a timestamp; otherwise the verified delivery ID is mandatory
monitorSecurity.rateLimit: Limit each repository identity to 60 requests per minute with a burst of 20 and the endpoint globally to 300 requests per minute. Return 429 on excess, record a security metric and alert on sustained rejection without publishing a Bus event
monitorSecurity.failureSemantics: Authentication, authorization, signature, replay, repository/ref validation and request-shape failures are fail-closed and never publish a Bus event. Return a non-2xx response and emit an audit event without logging secrets or payload values
monitorSecurity.audit: Record delivery ID, repository, ref, commit/revision, decision, rejection reason, target applications and resulting Bus event ID. Logs must exclude webhook secrets and configuration values and follow the corporate security-log retention policy

availabilityAndOperations.readiness: Config Server and clients are not ready when Kafka authentication, topic metadata or binding establishment fails during startup
availabilityAndOperations.runtimeOutage: Keep the last-known-good tracing configuration, report DEGRADED refresh delivery, retry broker connectivity with bounded exponential backoff and never synthesize a permissive configuration
availabilityAndOperations.recovery: After reconnect, each service obtains a complete authoritative snapshot from Config Server before applying a new accepted state; Bus events are triggers, not state
monitoring: Kafka producer error and retry rate
Kafka consumer lag per instance-scoped group
Webhook authentication, replay and rate-limit rejection counts
Refresh APPLIED, UNCHANGED, STALE and REJECTED outcomes
availabilityAndOperations.sloProposal: 99.9% of authenticated refresh intents reach every healthy target instance within 60 seconds, measured over a rolling 30-day window
availabilityAndOperations.disasterRecovery: Topics and ACL policy are recreated from infrastructure as code. No Bus event backup is required because Config Server is authoritative and every recovery performs a complete snapshot reload

verificationRequiredBeforeProduction: Infrastructure-as-code review proves exact topic, replication, min ISR, retention and ACL settings
Packaged Config Server test proves invalid signature, replay, wrong repository/ref and rate-limit cases publish no Bus event
Packaged multi-instance test proves every instance receives one intent despite instance-scoped Kafka groups
Cross-environment negative test proves principals cannot read, write or join groups outside their environment
Broker outage and reconnect test proves LKG retention and complete-snapshot recovery
Duplicate and out-of-order test proves deterministic UNCHANGED or STALE outcomes
Actuator exposure test proves busrefresh, busenv, busshutdown and public monitor routes are unavailable
closureRule: Architecture and infrastructure owners approve this proposal, record approver identities and an approval reference, change status to CORPORATE_BUS_CONFIRMED and e6Status to READY_TO_CLOSE_E6, then execute every verificationRequiredBeforeProduction check. Approval closes the E6 design gate; production rollout remains blocked until verification evidence is green.
